newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops wound six Palestinians in clashes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops wound six Palestinians in clashes.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded six Palestinians on Saturday during street battles with stone-throwers in the West Bank city of Hebron, Palestinian witnesses said.
They said soldiers intervened after Jewish settlers and Palestinians threw stones at one another in an area of Hebron under Israeli security control.
"All of a sudden the soldiers started shooting at Palestinians wounding six, but their injuries were not critical," one Palestinian witness said.
The Israeli army said it was checking the report.
Witnesses said PLO police, confined to areas in Hebron under Palestinian control, were trying to turn back angry Palestinians to prevent further clashes with Israeli soldiers.

Hebron, a flashpoint of Arab-Jewish violence, has been the scene of daily clashes since Tuesday when a Jewish settler shot dead a Palestinian shopkeeper near a shrine sacred to Moslems and Jews that stands over the tomb of the biblical Abraham.
Israeli troops have clashed almost daily with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza since Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.

Khaled Mishaal, leader of the militant Islamic resistance Movement Hamas, called on Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip and in the diaspora to escalate popular resistance against Israel and vowed that his group would continue its struggle.
"The Zionist enemy understands only the language of force," Mishaal said in a statement issued on Saturday. "Let the popular intifada (uprising) escalate until Palestine is liberated."
